reason: The inspected applicant journey is substantially coherent. The public proposition immediately explains student-led, no-fee, semester-long consulting; Join explains eligibility, preparation and evaluated versus unscored events. Source distinguishes unavailable recruitment from unpublished dates. The mobile homepage capture has disciplined hierarchy, and the synthetic recovery capture presents readable changed-field comparisons and explicit choices. Application source distinguishes saving from submitting, protects uncertain acknowledgements, combines exact saved/browser fields and resets consent after conflict resolution. The actual dashboard source and SSR assertions correct the earlier anonymous-review claim: assigned reviewers may see the identifying original resume, and the received banner requires owned stored submitted state. These are meaningful improvements, not grounds to repeat stale objections. However, I cannot establish the broad world-class claim from local source, intercepted browser journeys and SSR. The complete authenticated preparation/upload/recovery/status journey, keyboard completion and consequential operator integrations remain unproven. Membership scheduling facts and approved engagement evidence are still missing. Release readiness is separately unproven because actual provider acceptance has not been supplied. This is a simulated AI applicant lens, not observed student task success.

findings.userImpact: A first-time student cannot determine whether membership fits classes, employment or other obligations before investing in applying; a separate Board conversation remains necessary.
findings.suggestedFix: Have the Board approve and publish a dated current-semester typical weekly range, mandatory times and peak-period expectations alongside preparation. Retain the honest unavailable statement until facts are approved; do not invent hours.
